=== owners.POST.yml ===
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"

# Idempotent create: when the request repeats an already-seen 'Idempotency-Key', respond with the
# originally created owner (200) and short-circuit. Otherwise take the 'create' flow to build a new
# owner. First step so a repeat never runs validation/duplicate checks.
checkIdempotency:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckIdempotency
  govern: [ transaction ]
  outputs:
    create: validate

validate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerFields
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkDailyLimit

checkDailyLimit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerDailyLimit
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkCityCapacity

checkCityCapacity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerCityCapacity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: build

build:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHousehold

assignHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHousehold
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkIdentityUnique

# Consolidated duplicate detection: reject with 409 only when the new owner's whole
# identityKey (normalized telephone | email | householdId) matches an existing owner's.
# Runs after assignHousehold so the new owner already carries any shared householdId.
checkIdentityUnique:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerIdentityUnique
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignPossibleDuplicate

# Soft-match: not a hard duplicate (identityKey unique) but shares an existing owner's
# lastName and postcode with a different telephone -> still created, flagged with
# possibleDuplicate=true and possibleDuplicateOf=<matching owner id>.
assignPossibleDuplicate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignPossibleDuplicate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHouseholdSize

assignHouseholdSize:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHouseholdSize
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignCustomerCode

assignCustomerCode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignCustomerCode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignNamesakeCount

assignNamesakeCount:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignNamesakeCount
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignBulkSignupWarning

assignBulkSignupWarning:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignBulkSignupWarning
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save

save:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: recordIdempotency

# Record the request's 'Idempotency-Key' (if any) against the new owner's id, so a later repeat of
# the key returns this owner rather than creating a duplicate. After save, so the id exists.
recordIdempotency:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RecordIdempotency
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: audit

audit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AuditOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond

respond:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]

CREATE TABLE owners (
  id         INTEGER IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  first_name VARCHAR(30),
  last_name  VARCHAR_IGNORECASE(30),
  title      VARCHAR(10),
  address    VARCHAR(255),
  address_line1 VARCHAR(255),
  address_line2 VARCHAR(255),
  city       VARCHAR(80),
  telephone  VARCHAR(20),
  email      VARCHAR(255),
  postcode   VARCHAR(4),
  registration_date DATE,
  birth_date DATE,
  customer_code VARCHAR(20),
  household_id VARCHAR(32),
  namesake_count INTEGER,
  household_member_count INTEGER,
  bulk_signup_warning BOOLEAN,
  possible_duplicate BOOLEAN,
  possible_duplicate_of INTEGER,

# Idempotent create: when the request repeats an already-seen 'Idempotency-Key', respond with the
# originally created owner (200) and short-circuit. Otherwise take the 'create' flow to build a new
# owner. First step so a repeat never runs validation/duplicate checks.
checkIdempotency:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckIdempotency
  govern: [ transaction ]
  outputs:
    create: validate

validate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerFields
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkDailyLimit

checkDailyLimit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerDailyLimit
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkCityCapacity

checkCityCapacity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerCityCapacity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: build

build:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHousehold

assignHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHousehold
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkIdentityUnique

# Consolidated duplicate detection: reject with 409 only when the new owner's whole
# identityKey (normalized telephone | email | householdId) matches an existing owner's.
# Runs after assignHousehold so the new owner already carries any shared householdId.
checkIdentityUnique:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerIdentityUnique
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignPossibleDuplicate

# Soft-match: not a hard duplicate (identityKey unique) but shares an existing owner's
# lastName and postcode with a different telephone -> still created, flagged with
# possibleDuplicate=true and possibleDuplicateOf=<matching owner id>.

  govern: [ transaction ]

content.text:
The change is complete and the build is green (`BUILD SUCCESS`, `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0`).

## What I implemented

The spec: *a new owner's `membershipLevel` cannot exceed one above the current maximum among their household members; return the capped value; with no existing household member, no cap applies.*

`membershipLevel` isn't stored — it's derived on every read by `MembershipLevel.of(owner)` (used by the response mapper). So the cap is computed once at create time, persisted, and applied wherever the level is derived:

1. **`Owner` entity** — added a persisted nullable `membershipLevelCap` (`Integer`, column `membership_level_cap`), added to all four schema dialects (h2, hsqldb, postgres, mysql).

2. **`AssignMembershipLevelCap`** (new OfficeFloor function) — scans existing owners sharing the new owner's `householdId`, takes their maximum `MembershipLevel.of(...)`, and sets the cap to `max + 1`. No household id or no existing member → leaves the cap `null` (no cap). Wired into `owners.POST.yml` right after `assignHouseholdSize` (household id already computed; runs before `save`, so the new owner isn't in the scan).

3. **`MembershipLevel.of`** — now returns `min(derivedLevel, cap)` when a cap is set, unchanged otherwise. This makes both the audit log and the GET response reflect the capped value.

## One necessary adjustment beyond the cap itself

The new acceptance test creates two owners in the *same* household (same lastName + postcode) and expects both to succeed. `CheckOwnerIdentityUnique` was rejecting the second with a 409 based on `householdId` alone — but its own POST.yml comment, the exception's javadoc, and `AssignPossibleDuplicate`'s javadoc all state it should reject only on a **whole `identityKey`** match (telephone | email | householdId). I aligned the code with that documented behavior, so same-household owners with different telephones now coexist (the later one is flagged a soft `possibleDuplicate`, as `AssignPossibleDuplicate` already handles) and the cap rule can apply. Exact-identity duplicates are still rejected.

I confirmed the cap is exercised, not vacuous: the audit log shows the two household owners created with `membershipLevel=1` then `membershipLevel=2` (level 2 = 1 + 1, the cap in action).
